issues: Re-read driver (wf_load_uncertainty.py) + model.py and re-ran: reproduces reported numbers EXACTLY (control max|diff|=0.00e+00; naive 3.0353, pv_only 2.8335, pv_load 2.8050; edge_widens=YES). Checked specifically for the named bug classes. (1) CONTROL is NOT vacuous but IS weak: at load_spread=0, pv_load's three load arrays collapse to lf,lf,lf identical to pv_only AND its PV scenarios are identical to pv_only, so it confirms routing per-scenario load via paths 3-tuples equals the load[t] fallback. It would catch a load-plumbing/array-corruption bug, but it is near-tautological at the LP level (deterministic LP, identical inputs) so it cannot certify much beyond wiring. (2) NO baseline-equals-another bug: naive (1 scenario, P50 PV, inferred-P50 load) is structurally distinct from the 3-scenario controllers and clearly costlier; the ladder naive->pv_only->pv_load changes exactly one thing per step (PV scenario count, then load band) so attribution is clean. (3) NO over-hedging/implausible monotonicity: the pv_load-vs-pv_only mean win is small (+0.20%) and the day-level win rate is ~coin-flip (28/60), the expected modest hedge signature, not a suspiciously large universal gain. The committed t=0 step uses TRUE current load/PV in all modes (no look-ahead asymmetry). Seed sweep (5 seeds x 40 days): control held at 0.0 every seed; pv_load mean edge over pv_only was POSITIVE on all 5 seeds (+0.019..+0.043), so the mean-edge sign is robust, not an alternate-optima fluke. ONE OVERSTATEMENT in the prior takeaways/caveats: the worst-day tail improvement (8.66->8.43) is presented as a signature of the hedge, but across seeds the worst-day direction is MIXED (pv_load sometimes marginally WORSE in the tail), so that tail-improvement is partly seed-specific. The ROBUST effect is the small mean/expected-cost edge; the tail framing should be softened. This does not change the PASS or the YES verdict.
final_takeaways: VERIFIED & REPRODUCIBLE: driver re-run matches the report bit-for-bit (control 0.00e+00, naive 3.0353 / pv_only 2.8335 / pv_load 2.8050, edge_widens=YES). The control is valid (not vacuous) though weak, and there is no baseline-equals-another, band-collapse, or over-hedging bug. Result is trustworthy.
Phase 2 (stochastic, 3-scenario) clearly beats the naive P50-only baseline either way: PV-only +16.34% and PV+load +16.99% mean per-day saving vs naive. That gap is large and is the real headline.

Adding LOAD uncertainty WIDENS the edge, but only modestly and on the MEAN: PV+load is +0.20% of pv_only cost cheaper on average and cheaper on just 28/60 days (~coin flip). A 5-seed sweep confirms this mean edge is POSITIVE on every seed (+0.019..+0.043), so the direction is robust even though the per-day outcome is close to even.

CORRECTION to the prior framing: the worst-day tail improvement (8.66->8.43) is NOT robust. Across seeds the worst-day moves both ways (pv_load sometimes marginally worse in the tail). Read the PV+load benefit as 'a small, robust reduction in EXPECTED cost from modelling the coupled low-PV/high-load shock', NOT as a reliable tail-risk reducer. The honest one-liner is 'widens the mean edge slightly', dropping the tail emphasis.

Caveat stands and dominates the magnitude: this is a stylised single-battery/single-deferrable LP, not EMHASS, and the +0.20% PV+load edge scales directly with the ASSUMED PV-load anti-correlation (k=0.6), load band widths, and load_spread=0.30 - none fitted to real data. Treat the marginal PV+load value as directional and lower-bound; it could grow with stronger real coupling or shrink toward zero with weaker coupling.
